summary: Anne M. Blackburn specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Chicago under mentors Steven Collins and H. L. Seneviratne, later holding posts at Cornell University (2001–2006) and Harvard University (~2024).

Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of British Columbia, under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Lambert Schmithausen, Karin Preisendanz, and Geshe Tashi Namgyal. She held posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences (~2008).

Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield, Yutaka Hirata, Yukio Lippit, and Ryuichi Abe. She held visiting scholar posts at TNRICP, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.

Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Charles Hallisey (~1993–1999) and held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~2001).

Annemarie Schimmel was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1939–1941) and held posts at the universities of Marburg, Ankara, Bonn, and Harvard University (~1970–1992).
Annette Baier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (~1947–1952). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh from around 1973 to 1995.

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Vienna, learning under David Seyfort Ruegg and Christian Lindtner.

Annette Schmiedchen works in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Halle-Wittenberg, later holding academic posts at both institutions.

Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, where he later held a post from around 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~2000–2007) and became Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 2014.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak and held a professorship at Leiden University from 1947 to 1975.

Anthony Kennedy Warder worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS University of London under John Brough, and later held posts at the University of Edinburgh (~1955–1964) and the University of Toronto (~1964–1990).

Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Steven Collins, and at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.
Antoine Lutz works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University (~1997–2002), studying under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist, Iranologist, and Indologist. He studied at the University of Paris under Michel Bréal, Ferdinand de Saussure, and Sylvain Lévi, later holding posts at EPHE, ENLOV, and Collège de France (1906–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist, Iranologist, and historian. He held posts at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (1795–1838), the Collège de France (1806–1838), and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1822–1834).

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist who studied under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and the Collège de France as Professor of Indian Language (1814–1832).

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1831), where he later served as Privatdozent für orientalische Sprachen in 1849.

Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied law at Saint Petersburg State University (~1836–1840) and served as an academician at the Russian Academy of Sciences from around 1852 to 1879.
Anton Westermann was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1823–1826) and subsequently held a post there from around 1833 to 1869.
